This is a Sumerian mythological text describing primordial times and the creation/organization of the divine world. Here's my translation:

1. From distant days, when heaven and earth had been [fashioned],
2. From distant nights, when heaven and earth had been [fashioned],
3. From [distant] years, when destinies had been [determined],
4. When the Anunnaki had been born,
5. When the birth-goddesses had acquired (the power of) childbearing,
6. When the birth-goddesses had been distributed throughout heaven and earth,
7. When the birth-goddesses [...] had become pregnant and given birth,
8. When the gods' food rations [...] had been bound to their dining places(?),
9. When the numerous gods were at work, the lesser gods were bearing the workload,
10. When the gods were digging canals, heaping up their dirt on the banks,
11. When the gods were grinding(?), establishing the breath of life by command,
12. In those days, broad understanding (and) wisdom existed among the numerous gods,
13. Enki in the Engur, the deep well, the watery abyss - no god's heart could fathom that place,
14. He lay in his bedchamber, and sleep would not come upon him,
15. The gods were lamenting with tears, they were making lamentations,
16. To the one who lay asleep, his bed would not let him rise,
17. Namma, the primordial mother who gave birth to the numerous gods,
18. Brought the gods' tears to her son,
19. "You are truly lying down, you are truly sleeping,
20. [...] you do not rise,
21. The gods, your creatures, are smashing(?) their [...]"

Note: This appears to be part of a creation myth, possibly related to the story where the gods complain about their labor and Enki eventually creates humans to do the work. The text describes the primordial organization of the cosmos and the gods' distress at their laborious tasks.
